lines: Guiyang–Guangzhou HSR: east to Sanshui South/Guangzhou; north-west to Guangning/Guilin/Guiyang
Nanning–Guangzhou HSR: east to Sanshui South/Guangzhou; west to Zhaoqing West/Nanning
notes: The two lines share the eastern approach and diverge at Zhaoqing East, which the station article calls the junction station. The Guangzhou–Zhaoqing intercity uses Dinghu East and Zhaoqing stations instead. It adds another eastward route, but I did not count it as a separate direction.

lines: Qingdao–Rongcheng intercity railway (designed 250 km/h), main line: south-west to Taocun North/Laiyang/Qingdao; east to Muping/Weihai/Rongcheng. Also a Qingdao–Yantai direct branch to Zhifu and Yantai stations
Weifang–Yantai HSR (opened 2024-10-21, designed 350 km/h): west via Fushan to Penglai/Longkou/Weifang; ends at Zhifu, joining the Qingdao–Yantai direct branch
notes: Treated as one node: Yantai South, Zhifu and Yantai are all in urban Yantai. Three directions leave the city: toward Qingdao, toward Weihai, and toward Weifang. The Weifang–Yantai HSR terminates at Zhifu, which also makes Yantai a line end. I did not confirm whether a Weifang–Yantai train can run directly toward Muping without reversing. Yantai South closed for rebuilding on 2025-10-28, after the reference date.

lines: Shanghai–Kunming HSR: east to Yushan South/Hangzhou; west to Yiyang/Nanchang
Hefei–Fuzhou HSR: north to Dexing/Huangshan/Hefei; south to Wufushan/Wuyishan/Fuzhou
notes: A clean crossing of two through HSR lines, with no terminus. The Quzhou–Jiujiang line does not serve Shangrao station.

lines: Yinchuan–Lanzhou HSR: north to Lingwu North/Yinchuan; south to Hongsibu North/Zhongwei/Lanzhou
Yinchuan–Xi'an HSR: south-east to Baituguang/Qingyang/Xi'an North; ends at Wuzhong
notes: The track diagram marks the Yinchuan–Xi'an line's up and down termini at Wuzhong. Trains to Yinchuan share the Yinchuan–Lanzhou line north of here. I did not confirm design speeds on this page.

lines: Ningbo–Taizhou–Wenzhou railway (Hangzhou–Shenzhen corridor): north via Wenzhou North to Taizhou/Ningbo
Wenzhou–Fuzhou railway: south via Ouhai to Fuzhou
New Jinhua–Wenzhou railway (opened 2015-12-26, designed 200 km/h): west to Qingtian/Lishui/Jinhua; ends at Wenzhou South
Hangzhou–Wenzhou HSR (opened 2024-09-06, designed 350 km/h): north-west via Nanxijiang to Yiwu/Hangzhou West; main line ends at Wenzhou North
notes: Treated as one node: Wenzhou South and Wenzhou North are both in Wenzhou. The Hangzhou–Wenzhou HSR ends at Wenzhou North, and the Jinwen line ends at Wenzhou South. Both are line ends inside a 4-direction junction. The design speeds of the coastal Ningbo–Taizhou–Wenzhou and Wenzhou–Fuzhou lines were not re-checked on these pages.

lines: Jinan–Qingdao HSR: west to Qingzhou North/Jinan; south-east to Gaomi North/Qingdao
Weifang–Laixi HSR and Weifang–Yantai HSR (opened 2024-10-21): both leave north-east via Changyi, then split to Laixi and to Yantai
notes: The Weifang–Laixi and Weifang–Yantai lines share Changyi as their next station, so I counted them as one direction. The Tianjin–Weifang and Weifang–Suqian HSRs were under construction.

lines: Hangzhou–Ningbo HSR (Hangzhou–Shenzhen corridor): west to Hangzhou South; east to Shaoxing East/Ningbo
Hangzhou–Shaoxing–Taizhou HSR (opened 2022-01-08): shares the line west to Hangzhou; south-east to Shangyu South/Shengzhou/Taizhou
notes: The Hangzhou–Taizhou line branches off at Shaoxing North.

lines: Shantou–Shanwei HSR (Shantou South–Shanwei opened 2023-12-26, designed 350 km/h): west via Chaonan/Huilai/Lufeng to Shanwei, then on to Shenzhen and Guangzhou; on 2025-01-01 its eastern terminus was Shantou South
notes: On 2025-01-01, Shantou South was the stub terminus of the Shantou–Shanwei HSR, with one high-speed direction. Shantou station did receive D trains, but over the Chaoshan–Shantou link (designed 120 km/h, opened 2018-12-31), which is below the 200 km/h threshold. Chaoshan station is in Chaozhou, not Shantou. The Shantou–Shantou South link opened only on 2025-12-22. Shantou–Zhangzhou was not open.

lines: Xuzhou–Lanzhou HSR: east to Dangshan South/Xuzhou East; west to Minquan North/Zhengzhou
Shangqiu–Hefei–Hangzhou HSR (Shangqiu–Hefei opened 2019-12-01): south via Shangqiu East to Bozhou South/Fuyang/Hefei/Hangzhou; northern terminus is Shangqiu station
notes: Shangqiu station is both a junction and the line end of the Shangqiu–Hefei–Hangzhou HSR. The Xiong'an–Shangqiu section of the Beijing–Hong Kong HSR (to Caoxian West/Heze) opened only on 2026-09-28, so it is excluded. Counting it would give 4 directions now. The English station article is stale and still calls the Shangqiu–Hangzhou line 'planned'. The line article and the zh article settle it. Shangqiu East is an intermediate stop on the same line in the same city.

lines: Hainan Eastern Ring HSR: east/north-east via Yalong Bay to Wanning/Haikou
Hainan Western Ring HSR (opened 2015-12-30, 200 km/h): west via Phoenix Airport to Dongfang/Haikou
notes: The two ring lines formally terminate at Sanya, but they form one continuous island loop. About ten ring trains a day run Haikou East to Haikou East through Sanya. A train arriving from one side can only continue to the other side, so there is no routing choice. A literal reading of 'line_end' could apply, because both named lines end here.

lines: Nanning–Qinzhou HSR: north to Nanning
Qinzhou–Beihai HSR: south-east via Qinzhou East to Hepu/Beihai
Qinzhou–Fangchenggang HSR (opened 2013-12-30, designed 250 km/h): south-west via Qinzhou to Fangchenggang North
notes: The three branches of the Guangxi coastal network meet at Qinzhou North, where the Fangchenggang line leaves the Nanning–Beihai line. I did not confirm the design speeds of the Nanning–Qinzhou and Qinzhou–Beihai sections here.

lines: Hangzhou–Ningbo HSR (part of the Hangzhou–Shenzhen corridor): west via Zhuangqiao to Shaoxing/Hangzhou
Ningbo–Taizhou–Wenzhou railway (Hangzhou–Shenzhen corridor): south-east via Ningbo East to Taizhou/Wenzhou
notes: Ningbo station is an intermediate station on the combined Hangzhou–Shenzhen railway, though the Hangzhou–Ningbo HSR formally ends here. Excluded lines: the Xiaoshan–Ningbo conventional line; the Ningbo–Yuyao intercity, a conventional service; and the Ningbo–Jinhua railway (opened 2023-12-31), designed for 160 km/h. The Ningbo–Zhoushan and Nantong–Suzhou–Jiaxing–Ningbo lines were under construction.

lines: Hengyang–Liuzhou intercity railway: north-east to Liuzhou West/Guilin/Hengyang East; ends at Liuzhou
Liuzhou–Nanning intercity (passenger) railway: south-west to Jinde/Nanning
notes: Two separately named lines meet end to end here. Trains run through between Guilin and Nanning, so Liuzhou is the end of neither corridor and offers no routing choice. The Liuzhou–Wuzhou railway is excluded for two reasons: it was still under construction in June 2026, and it is designed for 160 km/h. The Guiyang–Nanning HSR runs via Hechi, not Liuzhou. Strictly, the Hengyang–Liuzhou line terminates here, so a literal reading of 'line_end' could apply. I chose through_stop because the corridor continues.

lines: Nanchang–Jiujiang intercity railway: south via Lushan to Nanchang; ends at Jiujiang
Anqing–Jiujiang HSR (listed as the Hefei–Jiujiang HSR): north across the Yangtze to Huangmei/Anqing/Hefei; ends at Jiujiang
Quzhou–Jiujiang railway (designed 200 km/h, D trains): east to Hukou/Jingdezhen/Quzhou; starts at Jiujiang
notes: Three directions confirmed. The Wuhan–Jiujiang passenger railway would add a westward direction, but I did not confirm it on these pages and left it out. The Quzhou–Jiujiang line just meets the 200 km/h threshold.

lines: Shanghai–Kunming HSR: north-east to Yiwu/Hangzhou; south-west to Longyou/Quzhou

New Jinhua–Wenzhou railway (金丽温, opened 2015-12-26, designed 200 km/h): south-east via Jinhua South to Wuyi North/Lishui/Wenzhou South; joins the Shanghai–Kunming corridor at Dongxiao (东孝) in Jindong District
notes: Treated as one node: Jinhua station (Shanghai–Kunming HSR) and Jinhua South station (Jinwen line) are both in urban Jinhua and connect through the Dongxiao junction. The Hangzhou–Wenzhou HSR runs via Yiwu, not Jinhua. The Ningbo–Jinhua railway (opened 2023-12-31) is designed for 160 km/h and is excluded. The Jinhua–Jiande HSR was not open.

lines: Nanjing–Hangzhou HSR: north to Changxing/Nanjing; south to Deqing/Hangzhou East
Shangqiu–Hefei–Hangzhou HSR / Huzhou–Hangzhou railway: north-west to Anji/Hefei; south to Deqing/Hangzhou West
Shanghai–Suzhou–Huzhou HSR (opened 2024-12-26, designed 350 km/h): east via Huzhou East to Nanxun/Suzhou South/Shanghai Hongqiao; ends at Huzhou
notes: The station article gives Deqing as the southern neighbour for both the Nanjing–Hangzhou and the Hefei–Hangzhou lines, so I counted the south as one direction. The Shanghai–Suzhou–Huzhou HSR opened six days before the reference date.

lines: Ganzhou–Shenzhen HSR at Huizhou North: north to Boluo North/Heyuan/Ganzhou; south to Zhongkai/Shenzhen
Guangzhou–Shanwei HSR (opened 2023-09-26) at Huizhou South: west via Boluo to Xintang/Guangzhou; east to Huidong/Shanwei; linked to the Ganzhou–Shenzhen HSR by the Mazhong and Huiluo connecting lines
notes: Treated as one node. The Guangzhou–Huizhou intercity yard at Huizhou North opened only on 2025-09-29, so it is excluded. Xiamen–Shenzhen railway service in Huizhou was not checked and not counted.

lines: Beijing–Guangzhou HSR (Wuhan–Guangzhou section): north to Hengshan West/Changsha; south to Leiyang West/Guangzhou
Hengyang–Liuzhou intercity railway (opened 2013-12-28, designed 250 km/h): south-west to Qidong/Yongzhou/Guilin/Liuzhou; starts at Hengyang East
Huaihua–Shaoyang–Hengyang railway (opened 2018-12-26, designed 200 km/h): west to Xidu/Shaoyang/Huaihua South; ends at Hengyang East
notes: Four directions. Two lines start here. The 200 km/h design speed of the Huaihua–Shaoyang–Hengyang railway comes from news reports, not Wikipedia.

lines: Guiyang–Guangzhou HSR at Guilin West: north-west to Wutong/Guiyang; south-east to Yangshuo/Guangzhou
Hengyang–Liuzhou intercity railway at Guilin North and Guilin: north to Lingchuan/Hengyang; south to Ertang/Liuzhou
notes: Treated as one node. A 6 km connecting line links Guilin West and Guilin North. The Hengyang–Liuzhou line runs at 200 km/h on the Yongzhou–Guilin section.

lines: Shangqiu–Hefei–Hangzhou HSR (Beijing–Hong Kong corridor): north to Taihe East/Bozhou/Shangqiu; south to Yingshang North/Huainan/Hefei
Zhengzhou–Fuyang HSR: west to Linquan/Zhoukou/Zhengzhou; ends at Fuyang West via a junction
notes: The Huainan–Fuyang and Fuyang–Huangmei lines were under construction or only partly open, so I did not count them.

lines: Harbin–Dalian HSR: north to Jinpu/Shenyang/Harbin; southern terminus at Dalian North

Dandong–Dalian intercity railway (opened 2015-12-17, designed 200 km/h): north-east via Jinzhou to Zhuanghe/Dandong; km 0 at Dalian North, with some trains continuing on the conventional line to Dalian station
notes: Dalian is the end of both corridors. The two lines diverge northward from Dalian North, so a train arriving from Shenyang can only reverse toward Dandong. That is not a meaningful onward choice. No other high-speed line serves Dalian.

lines: Shanghai–Kunming HSR: north-east to Zhuji/Hangzhou; south-west to Jinhua
Hangzhou–Wenzhou HSR (opened 2024-09-06): north to Pujiang/Hangzhou West; south to Hengdian/Wenzhou North
notes: A crossing of two through HSR lines. The Ningbo–Jinhua railway is excluded because it is designed for 160 km/h.

lines: Beijing–Guangzhou HSR: north to Gaobeidian East/Beijing; south to Dingzhou East/Shijiazhuang
Tianjin–Baoding intercity railway (Bazhou–Xushui section; opened 2015-12-28, designed 250 km/h): east via Baiyangdian to Bazhou West/Tianjin West
notes: Sources disagree on whether the Tianjin–Baoding line terminates at Baoding or Baoding East. The Baoding East article lists Baiyangdian as its neighbour on the Bazhou–Xushui line. Both stations are in Baoding city. The Xiong'an–Xinzhou and Shijiazhuang–Xiong'an lines were under construction.

lines: Zhangjiakou–Datong HSR: east to Yanggao South/Zhangjiakou/Beijing; ends at Datong South
Datong–Xi'an HSR: south via the Taishancun junction to Huairen East/Taiyuan; starts at Datong South
Ulanqab–Datong HSR (乌大高铁, formerly part of the Jining–Datong–Yuanping HSR; opened 2024-12-31, designed 250 km/h): north-west to Fengzhen North/Ulanqab; ends at Datong South
notes: Three directions, and all three lines terminate at Datong South. The Ulanqab–Datong line opened on 2024-12-31, one day before the reference date. Without it, Datong would be only a line end with 2 directions.

lines: Beijing–Shanghai HSR: north to Zaozhuang/Jinan/Beijing; south to Suzhou East (Anhui)/Bengbu/Shanghai
Xuzhou–Lanzhou HSR (Zhengzhou–Xuzhou section): west to Xiaoxian North/Shangqiu/Zhengzhou; section ends at Xuzhou East
Xuzhou–Yancheng HSR (opened 2019-12-16): east to Guanyin Airport/Suqian/Yancheng; starts at Xuzhou East
Lianyungang–Xuzhou HSR: north-east to Lianyungang; ends at Xuzhou East
notes: Five high-speed directions at one station. Three of the lines (Zhengzhou–Xuzhou, Xuzhou–Yancheng, Lianyungang–Xuzhou) terminate here, so it is also a line end. The Lianyungang–Xuzhou terminus is inferred from the station article's navbox order.

lines: Qinhuangdao–Shenyang HSR: west to Linghai South/Jinzhou; north-east to Tai'an/Shenyang
Panjin–Yingkou HSR: south-east via Panjin to Haicheng West/Harbin–Dalian HSR; starts at Panjin North
notes: The station article gives no direction arrows for the Panjin–Yingkou line. I inferred its direction from the line name and its station order.

lines: Qingdao–Yancheng railway (opened 2018-12-26, 200 km/h): north to Ganyu/Rizhao/Qingdao; south to Haizhou/Yancheng
Lianyungang–Xuzhou HSR: west to Donghai/Xuzhou East; terminates at Lianyungang
notes: The station article does not show where the Lianyungang–Zhenjiang HSR connects. It probably joins southward, but I did not count it separately.

lines: Datong–Xi'an HSR: north to Taiyuan South; south-west to Taigu West/Pingyao/Xi'an
Zhengzhou–Taiyuan HSR (Taiyuan–Jiaozuo section): north to Taiyuan South; south-east to Taigu East/Changzhi/Zhengzhou
notes: The two lines share the northern approach to Taiyuan South and diverge south of Jinzhong. That gives 3 directions and a real routing choice for southbound trains.

lines: Xuzhou–Lanzhou HSR, Xi'an–Baoji section (opened 2013-12-28): east to Qishan/Xi'an
Xuzhou–Lanzhou HSR, Baoji–Lanzhou section (opened 2017-07-09): west to Dongcha/Tianshui/Lanzhou
notes: Only one high-speed corridor, the Xuzhou–Lanzhou HSR, passes through. The Xi'an–Baoji and Baoji–Lanzhou sections were built separately and meet here, but trains run through and the corridor does not end. Platforms reserved for the Guanzhong intercity have no service. No other high-speed line serves Baoji. The Xi'an–Chengdu HSR bypasses it.
